content:
It may make sense to move the discussion on the PRs introducing heights and their properties from #maths > thoughts on elliptic curves @ 💬 to a dedicated thread in this channel.

#34330 is the third PR; its main part proves bounds for the height of a sum (of two or arbitrarily many field elements). It also adds positivity extensions for the various kinds of heights and adds a few API lemmas for products on Multisets and on finprods. One of these leads to a significant import increase in Mathlib/Algebra/BigOperators/Finprod.lean (it is not a public import, however). The alternative would be to put finprod_le_finprod into a new file (#find_home! didn't find a good place for it). This can be discussed in the PR comments.

I finally had some time to look at this.

Could you split the positivity extension into a separate PR?

And maybe all the API lemmas into another one? (Those parts are probably a quick merge.)
@Johan Commelin Done. #34533 contains the API lemmas.
... and #34534 the positivity extensions. I hope I have set up the dependency correctly.
Dependency setup looks good. Only think I did was put those references below the --- fold. So that they don't end up in the final commit message on master.
@Anne Baanen Could you have a quick look at #34534 again?
#34330 can now be looked at again; the dependencies have been merged.

#34776 just changes the name of "NumberTheory.Height.Instances" to "NumberTheory.Height.NumberField". So far, this file contains the docs#Height.AdmissibleAbsValues instance for number fields and already some number field specific results on heights. As I anticipate adding more number field specific results in the future, I think it makes sense to have a dedicated file for that. (After the move, the module docstring needs some updating, and the TODOs should be moved to the Basic file. I will do this in a follow-up PR, once this is merged.)

#34780 adds a new file "NumberTheory.Height.Projectivization" that contains the definition of multiplicative and logarithmic height of points in projective space, plus basic properties and positivity extensions analogous to those for heights of field elements and tuples.

I'm putting this into a separate file since I expect the "Basic" file to grow quite a bit over time and I also expect that quite some material will be added on the projective side (the goal would be to prove Weil's "Height Machine" eventually).
@Johan Commelin Is it OK if I assign you to #34330? You already had looked at it.
@Johan Commelin I've made the assignment now. Feel free to unassign yourself again.
Sorry, had very little review time this week. But I'll look at this next week. Thanks for the ping.

@Johan Commelin Can I ping you again on #34330 (and possibly also #34780)?
I have some more PRs in the pipeline and would like to have this in first.

The PRs mentioned in the next few posts are independent of the two mentioned above.

#35258 is one of a few PRs that adds API lemmas, in this case one lemma (now two lemmas) for docs#Finsupp.

#35259 adds two API lemmas for multivariate polynomials, an API lemma for docs#Polynomial.homogenize, and a definition (homogenize a polynomial map on the affine map to a polynomial map on the projective line) with some API for it.

#35260 adds convenience API lemmas for ciSup/ciInf-related statements in the case when the indexing type is finite (and so the boundedness condition is automatic). It then uses them to golf a few proofs.
Unfortunately, I'm short on time. Hopefully others can step in.
I will have a look later this week.
I had made one suggestions on one of the files. I had a look at all the other, and found nothing interesting to add. This looks good to me.
@Antoine Chambert-Loir It may perhaps help to leave an approving review.
#35407 does some minor stuff in NumberTheory.Height.Basic (fix names, add to_fun, add two API lemmas for docs#Height.logHeight parallel to existing ones for docs#Height.mulHeight).

#35408 adds more interesting material:

  • {mul|log}Height_comp_le: the height of x ∘ f is bounded by the height of x
  • {mul|log}Height_fun_mul_eq: the height of the "multiplication table" fun (i, j) ↦ x i * y j is the {product|sum} of the heights of x and of y
  • {mul|log}Height_fun_prod_eq: the analogous result for products with arbitrarily many factors
#35918 adds the descent theorem (which is needed to combine the various ingredients into the final proof).
#35919 adds the formula for logHeight₁ in terms of positive parts of logarithms.
#35922 adds some simple statements on heights of tuples index by subsingletons / obtained by extending a given tuple by zero.
#35923 adds height bounds for products (of tuples and field elements).
#35924 adds some lemmas on totalWeight for number fields and a positivity extension for it.
#35925 adds a new file with (for now) an upper height bound for the image under a linear map.
#35927 continues by adding upper height bounds for polynomial maps to NumberTheory.Height.MvPolynomial.
#35940 adds lower height bounds for polynomial maps.
#35941 adds (upper and lower) height bounds for ![x*y, x+y, 1].
#36222 is very small; it adds two API lemmas saying the inversion map is (strictly) antitone on positive elements.
#36223 adds some more API for docs#Function.HasFiniteMulSupport .
#36227 adds some lemmas about when subgroups/submodules have finite index.
#36229 adds two lemmas expressing Ideal.span (Set.range x) in different ways.
#36232 adds a version of Nat.cast_finprod that allows infinite index types.
#36233 adds three API lemmas related to multisets.
#36381 adds API for multiplicities in docs#UniqueFactorizationMonoid s.
#36458 adds some more API around docs#powMonoidHom and its additive counterpart.
#36494 (which depends on the previous one) adds more API related to finite index and multiplication-by-n.
#36986 (split off from the original version of a previous PR) adds simp lemmas for heights of tuples.

#36988 begins a sequence of PRs aimed at establishing the reduction of the Mordell-Weil Theorem (for an elliptic curve over a field with the Northcott property) to the weak Mordell-Weil Theorem. It introduces an avatar of the x-coordinate map from the elliptic curve to the projective line, plus some API.

#36989 is the next PR on elliptic curves. It defines the "addition-and-subtraction map" on x-coordinates of paris of points on an elliptic curve and proves a height inequality. (That the polynomial map defined in this way really comes from addition and subtraction will be shown in a later PR.)
#38183 adds well-known formulas for heights of tuples of rational numbers and of rational numbers.
#38648 is a small PR that adds two lemmas to the Northcott file (deduce that a composition is Northcott when one of the functions is Northcott and the other one satisfies some condition).
#38654 is the next step on the way to the Northcott property for heights on number fields. It adds API for ideal factorizations in Dedekind domains.
#39008 adds some more factorization API (and depends on the previous PR).
#39010 adds two convenience API lemmas for log and exp on real numbers.

#38654 has two approving reviews and an assignee (@Johan Commelin as of a couple of days ago), but no action since my last edits on Monday. Can we get it moving again? It is blocking further development on the way to the Northcott property for number fields.
#39118 (does not depend on the other PRs) adds some more API involving (relative) indices and ideals.

#39127 (depends on 39008) adds a lemma that shows that the product over the finite places in the multiplicative height of a tuple is the inverse of the absolute norm of the ideal generated by its entries.

#39181 is just a chore PR that moves the code for the positivity extension for docs#NumberField.totalWeight higher up in the file, so that we can later add code that uses it before the section on heights over the rationals.

#39193 is another chore PR. It moves the existing NumberTheory.Height.Northcott file to a new location Order.Northcott (its content is not number theory-specific) and uses the old location to add a height-specific instance.
The file move was split off to #39215.
Once #39008, #39127 and #39193 are merged, the Northcott property for number fields is only one last PR (with ~200 loc) away...
#39744 is now the promised PR that completes the proof of the Northcott property. It depends on 39127 (which adds one number field lemma and an API lemma).
How do you plan (if you do) to address the extension to points of bounded height and bounded degree?

I'm certainly planning to do this eventually. The first thing to do here is to define absolute heights (possibly for arbitrary algebraic elements in field extensions where the base field has a height theory). This in turn will require proving that the top field in a finite field extension inherits a height from the bottom field and what the relation between these heights is. I think most of the necessary ingredients for this latter point are by now available, but some work will be needed to provide the necessary glue.

My more immediate goal is to get a proof of the Mordell-Weil Theorem for elliptic curves over number fields into Mathlib, so I'm going to focus on PRs related to heights on elliptic curves first.
The final Northcott PR #39744 is now ready for review.
The next PR on elliptic curves: #40303 (the previous one, no. 36989, on the "addition-and-subtraction map" has now been reworked to allow for general Weierstrass curves).

The next step on the way to the approximate parallelogram law: #40574 .
It defines a function giving the symmetric square of the x-coordinate map and adds some basic API for it.
:tada: Northcott for number fields is now known to Mathlib!
Congratulations @Michael Stoll A very nice milestone that you worked towards with many PRs!
:thank_you: Thanks for the warm words! The next goal is the approximate parallelogram inequality on elliptic curves...
